published_prior_art.cite: GabrielSachsSjolander2025 Results 1 and 3 cover two- and three-arm low-cardinality target contrasts; SongGuoChanRichardson2024 Theorem 1 assumes potential outcomes for every exposure level.
BalkePearl1997 gives the sharp binary-IV ATE response-type bounds.
GabrielSachsSjolander2025 studies the relevant contaminated/ill-defined off-target setting, but does not supply this exact response-type certificate.
Blackwell1953 supplies the experiment-comparison framework; the displayed likelihood factorization is a routine consequence once the quotient is established.
Blackwell1953 does not cover a parameter-dependent allocation nuisance, but the claimed minimax reduction is a direct convexification consequence of the factorization.
SongGuoChanRichardson2024 Theorem 4 gives finite-sample KL-projection inference under full exclusion; the new content is contingent on Theorem 1's target-only quotient.
Hoffman1952 and Li1993 provide generic feasible-fiber/right-hand-side Lipschitz theory; the quotient-specific application is incremental.
LevisBonviniZengKeeleKennedy2025 and generic local-asymptotic lower-bound methods cover neighboring regular endpoint theory, but not this quotient formulation.

Gafarov2025 gives regularized uniform inference for affine identified sets and LevisBonviniZengKeeleKennedy2025 gives margin/smoothing methods, neither an exact target-IV face-by-face minimax frontier with an adaptive attaining procedure.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 4 (thm:nuisance-minimax)
soundness_flags.one_line: For an arbitrary convex action space and arbitrary full-data rule, E_{eta0}[delta(N)|S] need not exist or lie in A, so delta0 and its risk are not defined without integrability/finite-risk and closed-barycentric action-space conditions.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Result 1 treats a two-level IV with two target levels and one potentially ill-defined or contaminated third level; Result 3 treats a three-level IV with two target levels and one such third level.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 13-15, Theorem 1; pp. 25-27, Section 6 and Theorem 4
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 1 characterizes the joint law of potential outcomes for all K exposure levels under its categorical IV models; Section 6 builds finite-sample KL confidence regions from the full arm laws P(X,Y|Z=z).

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 92(439), 1997
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives sharp nonparametric bounds on the average treatment effect under random assignment with imperfect compliance.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1904.00111, corroborating preprint for Journal of Econometrics 249 (2025) 105952
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies regularized support-value inference in affine identified models under explicit LICQ-style active-constraint conditions; it does not state a target-IV quotient or an exact kink minimax phase diagram.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2301.12106v4, corroborating preprint for JRSS B article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies covariate-assisted Balke-Pearl bounds, using a novel margin condition for efficient estimation and smooth approximations for non-smooth bound functionals.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Restrict thm:nuisance-minimax to measurable rules with finite risk/integrable actions and take A to be closed convex, or formulate rules as randomized actions so the conditional barycenter is always admissible.

State an explicit strict-containment comparison with both GabrielSachsSjolander2025 and SongGuoChanRichardson2024: give a concrete law admitted by the target-only saturated model but excluded by Song's full-exclusion model, and identify the published low-cardinality subclass embedded in the quotient class.
Replace the generic regular-face citations with a precise parametric-LP regularity condition and source, then separate the regular-face lower bound from the genuinely open all-kink adaptive frontier.

recommended_next_step: Repair the decision-theoretic domain in Theorem 4, then advance the quotient theorem and its finite-sample consequence as the field-tier kernel.
